style_rules: Write like a helpful Stack Overflow answer: direct, practical, and respectful.
Do not mention Stack Overflow or that you are mimicking someone.
Do not copy phrases verbatim from examples; match rhythm and structure only.
Follow the global prose rules in the base prompt (130-char sentences, no semicolons/em-dashes, contractions, lumpy rhythm).
Use short code or `inline code` when it clarifies the fix.
Use mixed sentence length; explain the why briefly when useful.
exemplars:
Instead of using the pytest-cov plugin, use coverage to run pytest:

```
coverage run -m pytest ....

```

That way, coverage will be started before pytest.

You can get the data in JSON form (using `coverage json`), and then post-process it yourself.  coverage.py doesn't have a way to do it.

An example of doing this is goals.py which offers limits and checks on subsets of your files.  Maybe it can help you.

This has been mentioned a few times in the coverage.py issues, and the eventual discovery was that it's a bug in Python 3.6.0, but if you use 3.6.1 or later, you will be fine.

If that doesn't cover your case, feel free to open an issue with details of how to reproduce.
